newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rupiah may weaken on corporate debt problems - UBS.
newsitem.headline: Rupiah may weaken on corporate debt problems - UBS.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah, which fell to a historic low against the dollar earlier this week, is likely to come under further pressure as the corporate sector is facing debt problems, UBS Research said on Thursday.

"There is evidence that more Indonesian corporates are facing difficulties in rolling over their maturing foreign liabilities," the group said in a report, pointing to higher risk premiums and possibly lower credit limits because of falling investor confidence in nations with large current account deficits.
"As a result, more Indonesian corporates will have to buy rupiah and convert into foreign currency domestically," it said.
"Unless supported by strong intervention from Bank Indonesia, this will add pressure to the rupiah."
The rupiah was volatile on Thursday on a spillover of regional currency weakness.
It opened at 2,575/85 to the dollar, plunged to a low of 2,625 and was trading at 2,586 in the late afternoon.
On Monday, the rupiah plunged to a historic low of 2,665 to the dollar after a fierce speculative attack but recovered marginally on central bank intervention.
UBS said further weakness in the rupiah was likely to continue for the next three to six months.
Noting that the weakness was triggered by contagion from the Thai baht, it said: "Markets will take time to correctly assess the fundamental differences between the Indonesian and Thai economies."
"The baht was attacked because of the perception that the rigid exchange rate regime was inconsistent with sharply dropping economic activity and high domestic interest rates," UBS said.
"Conditions are different in Indonesia, which has a much more flexible foreign exchange system, robust economic activity and ample liquidity in the financial system."
